info.title: BigFatFile API
info.description:
The one public API of a BigFatFile Origin.

## Errors

Every error response has a JSON body in the problem details format (RFC 9457), with the content type `application/problem+json`. The `ProblemDetails` schema describes its fields. A client branches on `code`, never on `title`.

### Errors that any endpoint can return

- `bad_request`, 400: The request is not valid. The server could not read the request. For example, its JSON body is malformed, a required parameter is missing, or a parameter has a value that the spec does not list. Fix the request before sending it again.
- `invalid_fields`, 400: Some fields are not valid. The `errors` field lists what is wrong with each field.
- `authentication_required`, 401: This endpoint needs a token or a session. The request has no access token and no session cookie, or the one it has is not valid or has expired. Get a new token, or sign in again.
- `forbidden`, 403: The token or the session does not allow this. The request is authenticated, but its token does not have the scope that the endpoint needs. Ask for a token with that scope.
- `not_found`, 404: Nothing exists at this address. The resource does not exist, or the request has no access to it. The answer is the same in both cases, so it does not reveal what exists.
- `method_not_allowed`, 405: This address does not accept this HTTP method. The endpoint exists, but not with this HTTP method. The `Allow` header lists the methods that it accepts.
- `request_too_large`, 413: The request body is too large. Send a smaller body.
- `unsupported_media_type`, 415: This endpoint does not accept the content type of the request body. Send the body with a content type that the endpoint accepts, usually `application/json`.
- `server_error`, 500: The server failed to handle the request. Try again later. If the error does not go away, give the `traceId` to the server's operator.

### Errors of specific endpoints

Each endpoint lists its own errors under its responses, with an example body for each code. For example, see the responses of [Accept an invitation](#tag/account/POST/api/v1/account/invitations/accept).

get.description:
Returns a token that protects against cross-site request forgery (CSRF). In that attack, another website makes the browser send a request, and the browser adds the session cookie to it.

- Send the token in the `X-CSRF-Token` header of every POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE request that uses the session cookie.
- Get a new token after signing in or out, because each token belongs to one user.
- Requests with a bearer token do not need it.

429.description: `too_many_requests`: Too many requests from this address. Wait for the number of seconds in the Retry-After header. This IP address sent more requests than the endpoint allows in a period of time. Here, the limit is 20 sign-in attempts per minute from one IP address, for any accounts. All the addresses of one IPv6 /64 block count as one address.

get.summary: Sign in with an external account (OAuth)
get.description:
Sends the browser to the sign-in page of another service, such as Google or Microsoft. When the person has signed in there, the browser comes back to `returnUrl`, which must be a path on this server.

- `provider` is a `key` from `account.providers` in `GET /api/v1/meta`.
- The web app opens this address as a page in the browser, not with a fetch call, because the browser must follow the redirects.

post.description:
Creates an account with a name, an email address and a password.

- With `invitationToken`, the invitation email proves that the person receives mail at the address. The account is created at once, joins the invited tenant, and its session starts. The outcome is `signed_in`.
- Without it, a confirmation email is sent. The account can sign in once the address is confirmed. The outcome is `confirmation_sent`.
- When the address already has an account, the outcome is also `confirmation_sent`, and that account gets an email saying so. This way the response does not reveal which addresses have accounts.

post.description:
Confirms the address with the user ID and the code from the confirmation email, and starts a session. The link in the email opens the web app, which reads both values from it.

On a server with open sign-up, this is also when the person's new tenant is created.

Only the first confirmation of an address starts a session. So nobody can sign in later with a link that was forwarded or saved.

SignUpOutcome.description:
- `confirmation_sent`: a confirmation email is on its way. It is also the answer when the address already has an account, so the response does not reveal which addresses do.
- `signed_in`: the invitation proved the address, the account exists and its session has started.

SignUpPolicy.description:
- `invitation`: only people with an invitation can create an account.
- `open`: anyone can create an account, and gets a new tenant of their own.

invitationToken.description: The token from an invitation email. It proves the address, so no confirmation email is sent.

plan.description: The plan's key. The open core has one plan, `unlimited`.

TenantRole.description:
What a member may do in a tenant. Permission rules on drives and folders apply on top.
- `admin`: manages members, groups, drives and the tenant's settings, and is owner of every drive.
- `member`: may create drives, and sees the member list and the groups they are in.
- `guest`: has access only through the permission rules that name them, and sees neither the member list nor the groups.

oauth2.description: Tokens from this server's OpenID Connect endpoints. The web app on the same origin uses its session cookie instead.

scopes.shares.manage: Create and revoke share links on nodes the App may read.
scopes.members.manage: Invite and remove members, change roles, manage groups.
scopes.metadata.read: Read the App's own metadata namespace.
scopes.metadata.write: Write the App's own metadata namespace.
scopes.events.read: The change feed and the real-time hub.
scopes.apps.manage: The developer role: create Apps, rotate keys, see deliveries and usage.
scopes.tenant.admin: Tenant settings, warehouses, Replicas, audit and usage.
scopes.tenant.mirror: Every chunk and the whole change feed of the tenant, for mirroring and backup Apps.

session.name: bff_session

tags.name: account
tags.description:
The signed-in user, and the endpoints behind the web app's account screens: sign-up, sign-in, passwords and invitations.

- The web app calls them from the same origin as the server, with the session cookie.
- `GET /api/v1/account/me` also accepts a token with the `openid` scope, so Apps can call it too. The other endpoints do not accept tokens.
- Apps get their tokens from the OpenID Connect endpoints under `/connect`.

tags.name: tenants
tags.description:
The tenant, its members and its invitations.

- A token or a session works in one tenant. A request with any other tenant's ID gets 404, the same answer as for a tenant that does not exist.
- The endpoints that need the `members.manage` scope are for admins only. A user who is not an admin of the tenant gets 403 with the code `admin_required`.
- The endpoints that need the `members.read` scope are for members and admins. A guest of the tenant gets 403 with the code `member_required`.
